none: Paper dolls and paper outfits painted by Zelda Fitzgerald, cut out again

en: Derivative view of Beinecke MS 11873654 for the movable-books Cutout use case. Yale's copy of this object is already cut out, so their published manifest has one canvas per physical piece and no sheet at all. This manifest keeps that per-piece shape, and adds a leading derived canvas that lays the fourteen pieces back down on a virtual uncut sheet at the home positions recorded in the accompanying annotation page. Every image is still served by Yale: each piece is a region of its own Yale canvas, requested from Yale's IIIF Image service. Nothing is re-hosted here.

Read together with https://github.com/cubap/movable-books/blob/gh-pages/fixtures/pages/yale-11873654-paper-doll-annotations.json, which is the document the demo actually consumes, and with the live source manifest https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/11873654.

Paper dolls and paper outfits painted by Zelda Fitzgerald [graphic], ca. 1927. Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University, General Collection, MS 11873654. Images © Yale University Library; this derivative adds only descriptive metadata. See the catalog record for the current rights statement.
Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University
Paper-doll demo built on this object
Paper-doll model annotation page (roles, anchors, home positions)
Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library (New Haven, Conn.)
8 paper dolls (5 male, 3 female) and 6 paper outfits (4 men's, 2 women's); graphite, watercolor and gouache; 28-31 cm
14 recto/verso pairs, 28 canvases, served by Yale

All fourteen recto exposures are 3421-3468 x 5609 px, i.e. one fixed camera setup photographing pieces the catalogue measures at 28-31 cm. The pixel-to-millimetre ratio is therefore common to every piece, so an outfit can be laid on a figure at a 1:1 ratio with no resizing. A future instance mixing plates photographed at different magnifications would need a per-piece scale factor.

The first canvas is not a scan. It is a virtual rectangle 17090 x 11030 units, one unit per pixel of the Yale scans, onto which each piece is painted at its authored home position. It stands in for the uncut sheet this copy no longer has.
Derived uncut sheet (all fourteen pieces at their home positions)
Composed, not photographed. See the `sheet-model` annotation in the accompanying annotation page.
